stem: Find next two terms of an A.P. \(4, 9, 14, \ldots\)
solution: First term \(a=4\), common difference \(d=9-4=5\). Then \(t_4=a+(4-1)d=4+3\times5=19\) and \(t_5=a+(5-1)d=4+4\times5=24\). Hence the next two terms are 19 and 24.

stem: State whether the given equation is quadratic or not. Give reason. \(\dfrac{5}{4}m^2 - 7 = 0\)
solution: \(\dfrac{5}{4}m^2-7=0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{5m^2-28}{4}=0 \Rightarrow 5m^2-28=0\). The maximum index of the variable \(m\) is 2. Comparing with the general form \(am^2+bm+c=0\), we have \(a=5,\ b=0,\ c=-28\), which are real numbers with \(a\neq0\). Hence it is a quadratic equation in variable \(m\).

stem: If \(D_x = 25\), \(D = 5\) are the values of the determinants for certain simultaneous equations in \(x\) and \(y\), find \(x\).
solution: By Cramer's rule, \(x=\dfrac{D_x}{D}=\dfrac{25}{5}=5\).

stem: Write any one solution of equation \(x + 2y = 7\).
solution: Substituting \(x=1\): \(1+2y=7 \Rightarrow 2y=6 \Rightarrow y=3\). Hence \((1, 3)\) is a solution of the given equation.

subtopic: Sum of n Terms of an A.P.

stem: Find \(n\) if the \(n\)th term of the following A.P. is 64: \(1, 4, 7, 10, \ldots\)
solution: Here \(a=1\), \(d=4-1=3\), \(t_n=64\). Using \(t_n=a+(n-1)d\): \(64=1+(n-1)3 \Rightarrow (n-1)3=63 \Rightarrow n-1=21 \Rightarrow n=22\).

stem: If one of the roots of the quadratic equation \(x^2 - 10x + k = 0\) is 2, then find the value of \(k\).
solution: Since \(x=2\) is a root, it satisfies the equation: \((2)^2-10\times2+k=0 \Rightarrow 4-20+k=0 \Rightarrow -16+k=0 \Rightarrow k=16\).

stem: A box contains 20 cards marked with the numbers 1 to 20. One card is drawn at random, where the event A is such that the number on the card is multiple of 3. Write \(S\), \(n(S)\), \(A\) and \(n(A)\).
solution: \(S=\{1,2,3,\ldots,20\}\), so \(n(S)=20\). \(A\) = event that the number on the card is a multiple of 3 \(=\{3,6,9,12,15,18\}\), so \(n(A)=6\).

stem: Find the value of \(x - y\) if \(6x + 5y = 17\), \(5x + 6y = 13\).
If the roots of quadratic equation are 5 and \(-6\), form the quadratic equation.
solution: Let \(\alpha=5\) and \(\beta=-6\). Then \(\alpha+\beta=5+(-6)=-1\) and \(\alpha\beta=5\times(-6)=-30\). The required equation is \(x^2-(\alpha+\beta)x+\alpha\beta=0\), i.e. \(x^2-(-1)x+(-30)=0\), i.e. \(x^2+x-30=0\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem: For a certain frequency distribution mean is 72 and median is 78, find the mode.
solution: Let the mode be \(x\). Using the empirical relation Mean \(-\) Mode \(= 3(\)Mean \(-\) Median\()\): \(72-x=3(72-78)=3\times(-6)=-18 \Rightarrow x=72+18=90\). Hence the mode is 90.

subtopic: Solving by Formula and Completing the Square
stem: Solve the following quadratic equation by formula method: \(3x^2 + 2x = 1\)
solution: \(3x^2+2x-1=0\); comparing with \(ax^2+bx+c=0\), \(a=3,\ b=2,\ c=-1\). \(x=\dfrac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}=\dfrac{-2\pm\sqrt{(2)^2-4\times3\times(-1)}}{2\times3}=\dfrac{-2\pm\sqrt{4+12}}{6}=\dfrac{-2\pm\sqrt{16}}{6}=\dfrac{-2\pm4}{6}\). So \(x=\dfrac{2}{6}=\dfrac{1}{3}\) or \(x=\dfrac{-6}{6}=-1\). The roots are \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) and \(-1\).

stem: Solve the following simultaneous equations by using Cramer's rule: \(4x + 3y = 4\); \(6x + 5y = 8\)
solution: \(D=\begin{vmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ 6 & 5 \end{vmatrix}=20-18=2\neq0\), \(D_x=\begin{vmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ 8 & 5 \end{vmatrix}=20-24=-4\), \(D_y=\begin{vmatrix} 4 & 4 \\ 6 & 8 \end{vmatrix}=32-24=8\). Hence \(x=\dfrac{D_x}{D}=\dfrac{-4}{2}=-2\) and \(y=\dfrac{D_y}{D}=\dfrac{8}{2}=4\). So \(x=-2\) and \(y=4\).

stem: A die is thrown, find the probability of the event of getting a square number.
solution: Sample space \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\), so \(n(S)=6\). Let A = event of getting a square number \(=\{1,4\}\), so \(n(A)=2\). \(P(A)=\dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)}=\dfrac{2}{6}=\dfrac{1}{3}\).

stem:
The marks obtained by a student in an examination out of 100 are given below. The total marks obtained in various subjects are as follows. Represent the above data using a pie diagram.

| Subject | Marks |
|---|---|
| Marathi | 80 |
| English | 80 |
| Science | 100 |
| Mathematics | 100 |
| Total | 360 |
solution: Central angle for each subject \(=\dfrac{\text{marks}}{360}\times360^\circ\). Marathi: \(\dfrac{80}{360}\times360^\circ=80^\circ\); English: \(\dfrac{80}{360}\times360^\circ=80^\circ\); Science: \(\dfrac{100}{360}\times360^\circ=100^\circ\); Mathematics: \(\dfrac{100}{360}\times360^\circ=100^\circ\) (total \(360^\circ\)). Draw a circle and mark sectors of \(80^\circ, 80^\circ, 100^\circ, 100^\circ\) for Marathi, English, Science and Mathematics respectively.

stem: If \(\alpha + \beta = 5\) and \(\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = 35\), find the quadratic equation whose roots are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).
solution: Using \(\alpha^3+\beta^3=(\alpha+\beta)^3-3\alpha\beta(\alpha+\beta)\): \(35=(5)^3-3\alpha\beta(5)=125-15\alpha\beta\). So \(15\alpha\beta=125-35=90 \Rightarrow \alpha\beta=6\). The required equation is \(x^2-(\alpha+\beta)x+\alpha\beta=0\), i.e. \(x^2-5x+6=0\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
Frequency distribution of daily commission received by 100 salesmen is given below. Find the mean daily commission received by salesmen, by assumed mean method.

| Daily commission (in Rs.) | No. of Salesmen |
|---|---|
| 100 - 120 | 20 |
| 120 - 140 | 45 |
| 140 - 160 | 22 |
| 160 - 180 | 9 |
| 180 - 200 | 4 |
solution: Take assumed mean \(A=150\); deviation \(d_i=x_i-150\). Class marks \(x_i\): 110, 130, 150, 170, 190; deviations \(d_i\): \(-40, -20, 0, 20, 40\); frequencies \(f_i\): 20, 45, 22, 9, 4 with \(\sum f_i=100\); \(f_id_i\): \(-800, -900, 0, 180, 160\) with \(\sum f_id_i=-1360\). Then \(\bar d=\dfrac{\sum f_id_i}{\sum f_i}=\dfrac{-1360}{100}=-13.6\) and \(\bar x=A+\bar d=150+(-13.6)=136.4\). Thus the mean daily commission is Rs. 136.40.

stem: A boat takes 10 hours to travel 30 km upstream and 44 km downstream, but it takes 13 hours to travel 40 km upstream and 55 km downstream. Find the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the stream.
solution: Let the speed of the boat in still water be \(x\) km/h and the stream be \(y\) km/h. Then upstream speed \(=(x-y)\) and downstream speed \(=(x+y)\). Conditions: \(\dfrac{30}{x-y}+\dfrac{44}{x+y}=10\) and \(\dfrac{40}{x-y}+\dfrac{55}{x+y}=13\). Put \(m=\dfrac{1}{x-y}\), \(n=\dfrac{1}{x+y}\): \(30m+44n=10\) and \(40m+55n=13\). Solving these, \(n=\dfrac{1}{11}\) and \(m=\dfrac{1}{5}\). So \(x-y=5\) and \(x+y=11\); adding, \(2x=16 \Rightarrow x=8\), then \(y=3\). Thus the speed of the boat in still water is 8 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h.

Draw histogram and frequency polygon on the same graph paper for the following frequency distribution:

| Class | Frequency |
|---|---|
| 15 - 20 | 20 |
| 20 - 25 | 30 |
| 25 - 30 | 50 |
| 30 - 35 | 40 |
| 35 - 40 | 25 |
| 40 - 45 | 25 |
solution: On the X-axis mark the class intervals 15-20, 20-25, 25-30, 30-35, 35-40, 40-45 and on the Y-axis the frequencies. Draw adjacent rectangles (bars) of heights 20, 30, 50, 40, 25, 25 respectively to obtain the histogram. For the frequency polygon, join the mid-points of the tops of the bars in order, and close it by joining to the mid-points of the class just before the first (12.5) and just after the last (47.5), both at zero frequency, on the same graph.
